title: Stranded in Arizona, Eli Rice's tour and Monroe, Louisiana
summary: Moore, stuck in Arizona, joined Eli Rice's band, which broke up in Monroe, where he joined Ben Burton's local band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So when you finished with Lionel Hampton you were going to set out to conquer New York, is that the way it was?

Everybody asked me, said, why don't you go to New York. Go to New York. There's nothing here for you. Go to New York. So I got this little bread from my land in Arizona. I cut out, went to Arizona and didn't get to New York. I left my money with my folks and I got stranded there. And all the bands that came through to play at the Riverside Ballroom in Phoenix, I used to go hear until one time there was a band from Minneapolis by the name of Eli Rice and they heard of my reputation in California, so they said, 'well, come on with us. What are you doing here?' So I said, 'well, I want to latch onto somebody.' I needed the job so I left Arizona with Eli Rice and all the way through with the tours -- Shreveport, Texas and finally ended up in Monroe, Louisiana, and the band

busted up. We had to take the bus back to Minneapolis and we were all stranded there, some went home. I didn't go home and I stayed right in Monroe and I joined a local band by the name of Ben Burton. We played jobs around until a band from New Orleans came to play a dance in Monroe, and the gentleman's name was Oscar "Papa" Celestin.
